Article Title: CRPF to do post-analysis of RAF action in NEET protests, says DG; 47 RAF personnel injured
Article Text:
CRPF director general Gyanendra Pratap Singh

NEW DELHI: CRPF director general Gyanendra Pratap Singh on Saturday said the force would conduct a professional post-analysis of the action taken by personnel of Rapid Action Force (RAF), a unit of CRPF, against anti-NEET paper leak protestors, including during the July 20 march to Parliament.“Now, since agitation has been called off, and once assembled people disperse, we would make a professional post-event assessment, like we do after every major assignment, and then let you know of the view of force headquarters,” Singh told TOI on Saturday. This is the first official statement from CRPF in the wake of allegations that pellet guns were used against protestors during the July 20 march to Parliament.Three people have claimed to have suffered pellet injuries in the police action.At least 47 RAF personnel too sustained injuries, allegedly from violent elements in the protests.Sources said the post-event assessment by CRPF will go into all possible aspects of RAF deployment during the protests. This would include action taken by RAF personnel against the protestors, riot-control gear used by them and whether the ground situation justified it. It will examine if the RAF response was graded and in line with the standard operating procedures and riot control manual.An officer said the CRPF will also examine the provocation and aggression that the RAF personnel likely faced at the hands of external, motivated elements who may have infiltrated the protests.CRPF sources said of the 47 RAF personnel injured during the course of their deployment for protests in the Capital, six have sustained head injuries and four, fractures. An officer claimed RAF personnel were hit by protesters with iron rods, likely retrieved from damaged railings. The accounts of the personnel regarding how the injuries were sustained, will be recorded as part of the post-event analysis.Delhi Police had clarified that they do have any pump action guns (PAG), but these are part of RAF’s standard anti-riot gear, along with shock batons. The CRPF review will probe allegations of firing of pellets by any personnel on duty, and if such action was authorised, justified and part of a graded response.NEW DELHIPAG, commonly known as pellet gun, is classified as a 'non-lethal’ anti-riot measure. As per the standard RAF drill, it is to be used only as a second last resort, with police firing being the last. Any RAF anti-riot action should start with engagement with the protestors or unruly mob, followed by warning on public address system to disperse. If all this fails, water cannon or tear gas may be used. Pellet gun is the next level of force applied, and may be fitted with a muzzle deflector so that the pellets hit only the lower body, leaving vital organs unharmed.
Article Summary: Crpf director general gyanendra pratap singh on saturday said the force would conduct a professional post-analysis of the action taken by personnel of rapid action force. This is the first official statement from crpf in the wake of allegations that pellet guns were used against protestors during the july 20 march to parliament.

Article Title: Nepal seeks India's approval for biometric national identity card as travel document
Article Text:
Nepal seeks India's approval for biometric National Identity card as travel document (ANI image)

Nepal plans to replace citizenship certificates

India reviews the proposal

The Kathmandu Post

Nepal has formally requested India's approval to recognise its biometric National Identity (NID) card as an official travel document for cross-border journeys, alongside passports and citizenship certificates.At present, Nepali citizens travelling to India, particularly by air, must carry either a valid passport or an original citizenship certificate. Indian citizens entering Nepal are required to present either a passport or an original voter identity card with a photograph.However, Nepal's National Identity card contains biometric information, including fingerprints, facial images and iris scans. The programme was launched as a pilot in Panchthar district and among government employees in 2009.So far, more than 4.5 million Nepali citizens have received the card, while nearly 20 million applications have been submitted.The request comes as Nepal gradually makes the biometric National Identity card mandatory for banking, land registration, passport issuance and access to public services, with plans to eventually replace citizenship certificates."In the long run, we will have a single identity card replacing the citizenship certificate.It is verified, authentic and technology-friendly," Tiwari said."That is why we have requested India to allow the use of the National Identity Card while travelling by both air and land routes," he added.According to senior immigration officials quoted by, an Indian Embassy delegation met officials from Nepal's Department of Immigration earlier this week to discuss the proposalThe delegation was reportedly "positive" about the initiative and informed Nepalese officials that the request had been forwarded to authorities in New Delhi for consideration."We have already forwarded the proposal to the Indian side through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs," said Ram Chandra Tiwari, Director General of the Department of Immigration.Officials from Nepal's Home Ministry also said that discussions have included creating formal mechanisms to record cross-border travel data and better manage movement between the two neighbouring countries.
Article Summary: Nepal seeks india's approval for biometric national identity card as travel document. At present, nepali citizens travelling to india must carry either a valid passport or original citizenship certificate. Indian citizens entering nepal are required to present either a passport or an original voter identity card with a photograph.

Article Title: 'Rewarding corruption': CJP attacks Centre over education secretary's replacement
Article Text:
Education secretary's transfer triggers fresh CJP attack on Centre

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday alleged that the transfer of the Education Secretary amounted to "rewarding corruption instead of ensuring accountability". He claimed that the official had been replaced by an IAS officer from the Animal Husbandry Department who faces "severe multi-crore corruption charges"."Last night, the Education Secretary was transferred. He was replaced by an IAS officer from the Animal Husbandry Department who has severe multi-crore corruption charges against him. The entire crisis around paper leaks and NEET was about systemic corruption," Dipke said in a post on X.Abhijeet further said that replacing one bureaucrat with another facing "serious corruption allegations" was "a direct insult to young people across India".Questioning whether this was the "compromise" the government expected students to accept, he asserted that "this is not accountability" and said the protest would continue until Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns."Replacing one bureaucrat with another facing serious corruption allegations is a direct INSULT to young people across India.Is this the "compromise" the government expects us to accept? This is not accountability. We will not stop until Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns," Dipke added.The Centre on Thursday carried out a major bureaucratic reshuffle, making 13 secretary-level appointments across ministries and departments, including key changes in the education ministry, amid continuing protests over the alleged NEET paper leak.Senior IAS officer Naresh Pal Gangwar has been appointed Secretary, Department of Higher Education, while T K Anil Kumar has been named Secretary, Department of School Education and Literacy. According to an order issued by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC), Gangwar, a 1994-batch IAS officer of the Rajasthan cadre, will succeed Vineet Joshi as Secretary of the Department of Higher Education.The agitation over the NEET paper leak spread across several states on Friday, a day after CJP called for nationwide demonstrations. Protesters condemned the Delhi Police crackdown on July 20 and reiterated their demand for the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.As the protests gathered momentum across states, the Congress directed its state units to organise candlelight marches and 'satyagraha' in every district on Saturday evening to protest against the "irregularities in the NEET and CBSE examinations and the subsequent repressive actions by the Modi government".On Friday, a high-level meeting between leaders of CJP and senior BJP leaders, including Union Health Minister JP Nadda and Union Minister Jitendra Singh, was held at the Constitution Club in New Delhi.Earlier, activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike at Medanta Hospital in the presence Nadda and Jitendra Singh after the Union government gave a written assurance on the NEET examination issue and broader systemic reforms to the country's competitive examination framework.Meanwhile, Prime Minister Narendra Modi assured that strict action would be taken against those responsible for the alleged paper leaks. He also said the Union Cabinet would consider a draft Bill proposing fast-track courts and stricter punishment for offenders.
Article Summary: Education secretary's transfer triggers fresh cjp attack on centre. Cockroach janata party (cjp) founder abhijeet dipke on saturday alleged that the transfer of the education secretary amounted to "rewarding corruption instead of ensuring accountability" he claimed that the official had been replaced by an ias officer from the animal husbandry department who faces "severe multi-crore corruption charges"

Article Title: Army rescues 57 stranded as major flood relief operation begins in Gujarat's Navsari
Article Text: The Indian Army on Saturday rescued 57 people stranded by floodwaters at Tata High School on Ring Road in Gujarat's Navsari district as heavy rainfall continued to batter parts of the state. Seperately, Army personnel also evacuated vulnerable residents from Sanduri village in the Madhuban Dam area of Dadra and Nagar Haveli.The rescue operations were launched under the Army's humanitarian assistance and disaster relief initiative following distress calls from flood-hit areas.Responding to an emergency call, southern command deployed rescue teams to Sanduri village, where Army personnel worked in coordination with the civil administration and local volunteers to shift 23 vulnerable civilians to a designated relief shelter.The Army said medical assistance was provided on-site, while essential rations and relief supplies were distributed to residents who remained in the village. It added that relief and rescue operations were continuing across the affected areas.The flooding also disrupted road connectivity in Gujarat. The Ahmedabad district police announced the temporary closure of the Ahmedabad-Viramgam Highway after excessive water flow made the route unsafe."No vehicle from Sanand to Viramgam and Viramgam to Sanand is safe to ply over it. We are closing the entire highway for the time being," the Ahmedabad District Police said, according to news agency ANI.Ahmedabad district collector Bhavya Verma told the news agency that the authorities remained on high alert despite the situation being under control."We have also deployed Indian Army and SDRF teams along the Ahmedabad-Rajkot Highway. The situation is currently under control, though waterlogging persists in several areas. All administrative and rescue teams are actively deployed on the ground. A red alert for heavy rainfall remains in effect for Ahmedabad district tomorrow as well..." Verma told ANI.He said Dholka and Viramgam recorded the highest rainfall in the district over the past 24 hours, adding that rescue operations were being carried out with the assistance of the SDRF, police and the local administration.Meanwhile, Gujarat deputy chief minister Harsh Sanghavi visited flood-affected areas in Umargam of Valsad district on Friday, where he reviewed the situation, interacted with residents and urged people to avoid rumours and follow official advisories.Earlier this week, the NDRF rescued 67 people, including 25 women and 22 children, from floodwaters in Navsari's Sarikhurad village. In Tapi district, the SDRF rescued 11 stranded villagers, while in Surat more than 4,800 people from urban and rural areas were shifted to relief centres and safer locations as rescue operations continued.
Article Summary: The indian army rescued 57 people stranded by floodwaters at tata high school on ring road in navsari district. Army personnel also evacuated vulnerable residents from sanduri village in the madhuban dam area of dadra and nagar haveli. The rescue operations were launched under the army's humanitarian assistance and disaster relief initiative.

Article Title: 3 years on, SIT probe complete in just 10% of Manipur riot cases
Article Text: NEW DELHI: More than three years after Kuki-Meitei ethnic clashes singed Manipur and claimed 260 lives, Supreme Court was informed Friday that probes into only 10% of the 3,000-odd cases had been completed by SITs of state police while CBI had investigated the majority of the 31 cases referred to it.Appearing for the CBI, additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that the central probe agency had filed chargesheets in 21 cases and closure reports in six, of which three had been accepted. It was continuing investigations into the remaining four cases.Former Maharashtra DGP Dattatray Padsalgikar, who was appointed to oversee the investigations, informed the court through a report that of the 3,020 cases being probed by the SITs across eight districts, chargesheets had been filed in only 301 cases and trial had commenced in 10.The CJI-led bench told the investigators to act expeditiously. Given the volume of cases, SC mulled setting up special courts to try these exclusively. It sought responses to this from Manipur govt and the high courts of Assam and Manipur.SC had transferred investigations into cases of rape-murder other heinous offence to CBI and shifted their trial to Guwahati. The central agency told the court that examination of witnesses residing in Manipur through video-conferencing was a challenge because of law-and-order situations, non-cooperation and language barriers as they spoke different dialects.Senior advocate Ngangom Junior Luwang complained that no effort had been made to trace 30 missing people and without their remains, authorities were not issuing death certificates required for other purposes. SC asked him to approach Manipur high court.Advocate Sharukh Alam submitted that land belonging to churches vandalised during the clashes were getting encroached upon and said govt had taken no steps to reconstruct them. Bhati said govt's priority was to reconstruct damaged dwelling units. The bench said govt was right to prioritise reconstructing houses but asked it to take steps to stop encroachment of places of worship.
Article Summary: Only 10% of the 3,000-odd cases had been completed by sits of state police. Cbi had investigated the majority of the 31 cases referred to it. The cji-led bench told the investigators to act expeditiously.

Article Title: FIRs against protesters to be quashed, compensation to be given & 5-point Charter: What Centre, CJP said in joint press meet
Article Text:
The joint press conference was attended by Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, along with CJP national spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka and CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das. (PTI image)

What govt said:

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think the government response to the NEET paper leak was adequate? Yes, they acted swiftly No, they should have done more 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janata Party on Saturday withdrew its protest against the irregularities in education system including NEET paper leak at Jantar Mantar after the government agreed to its all its demands.In a joint press conference with Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh and the CJP delegation, CJP spokesperson Saurav Das said the decision was taken after an understanding that the terms would be implemented within the agreed-upon timeframe."Cockroach Janta Party declares that we withdraw the agitation in good faith, with the understanding that the agreed-upon terms will be executed within the agreed-upon timelines," Das said."All our demands have been accepted, so we request the protesters to withdraw immediately and return home peacefully. We will inform you of our future strategy or any other issues. But we request the protesters to withdraw immediately," he added.Meanwhile, Nadda said the government had accepted the demands presented by the delegation, including that no police action would be taken against the protesters and that compensation would be provided to the families of students who died by suicide, in accordance with the rules and regulations."We had a long conversation today. They brought a written draft in which they made four points about the ongoing cases in agitation. Along with that, we discussed the other two demands: no retaliatory measures should be taken, compensation should be provided, and their five-point charter should be considered," Nadda said."We will provide them with copies of the FIRs, and no action will be taken. The second thing that has been said is that regarding compensation, the government has clearly stated that we also sympathize. We all have said that there will be compensation according to the rules and regulations. Whatever maximum will be possible will be given to them," he added.On the five-point charter presented by the CJP delegation, Nadda said the government would "think deeply" about the suggestions for reforms in the education examination system."This five-point charter, which you gave me, is related to reforms in education examinations. Regarding it, we have to say that we will think deeply about your charter for reforms in education examinations and, after talking to your delegation, we will try to do whatever we can. So these were their demands. I think the government has sympathetically considered all the demands they had made and has also accepted them," he added.The Centre's agreement came a after Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned amid nationwide protests over the NEET paper leak.Pradhan said he had stepped down after considering the situation that had developed at Jantar Mantar and across the country, adding that the government had acted swiftly after irregularities in the NEET-UG examination surfaced by handing the probe to the CBI, cancelling the examination and announcing a re-test.Minutes after Pradhan's resignation, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke had declared that the protest would continue until the remaining demands were met. He had sought Rs 1 crore compensation for the families of students who died by suicide following the paper leak and action against police personnel over the alleged crackdown on protesters on July 20.However, following three rounds of talks with the Centre, the CJP on Sunday announced that it was withdrawing its 36-day agitation at Jantar Mantar with immediate effect after the government accepted its remaining demands, while also agreeing to consider the party's five-point charter on examination reforms.
Article Summary: The cockroach janata party on saturday withdrew its protest against the irregularities in education system including neet paper leak at jantar mantar. In a joint press conference with union ministers jp nadda and jitendra singh and the cjp delegation, cjp spokesperson saurav das said the decision was taken after an understanding that the terms would be implemented within the agreed-upon timeframe.

Article Title: Dharmendra Pradhan resigns: Government took exit call after Wangchuk breakthrough failed to end protests
Article Text:
Govt took exit call after Wangchuk breakthrough failed to end protests

NEW DELHI: BJP has fended off numerous opposition campaigns built around allegations, contentious laws or policies, and suspected wrongdoings of a senior Union minister or a chief minister since PM Modi took office in 2014 without making any appearance of bowing to pressure. However, where the opposition could not succeed, street protests and the fear that they could have triggered violence have.The resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan, a key member of the Cabinet since Modi first took office in 2014, following unebbing protests is a significant political dent to the party, presenting the opposition a rare opening to build on youth anger after suffering electoral setbacks and desertions from ranks.Govt hoped to benefit from the optics of activist Sonam Wangchuk breaking his 26-day hunger strike by accepting soup from Union minister J P Nadda and agreeing to the gentle terms built on assurances.With the protests, though, showing no signs of a let-up and Rahul Gandhi stepping up opposition's stir, BJP chose pragmatism over defiance, more so as it was confronted with Gen Z that did not deal in the old grammar of politics, making its irreverent slogans, memes and skits go viral.Earlier, government had withdrawn farm laws in Nov 2021 following a year-long protest from farmers, while Modi had publicly announced in Dec 2019 that his govt had no plans for a National Register of Citizens to defuse the agitation against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act.J Akbar, who quit in 2018 after his name surfaced in the #MeToo row, was a junior minister and carried little political heft. As BJP counts its losses, it will have to grapple with the challenge of winning over a generation which, many political observers say, had been showing signs of restiveness over a host of employment-related concerns even before these protests broke out, despite a section supporting the party’s other planks. The view within BJP is that despite the immediate political price it has paid, it has shown its sincerity of purpose by engaging with protesters and conceding to them, belying the charge that it was “arrogant and insensitive
Article Summary: Govt took exit call after wangchuk breakthrough failed to end protests. Govt hoped to benefit from the optics of activist sonam wangchuk breaking his 26-day hunger strike by accepting soup from union minister j p nadda. With protests showing no signs of a let-up, rahul gandhi stepped up opposition's stir.

Article Title: Pralhad Joshi, man with a low profile & an effective style
Article Text:
Pralhad Joshi named new education minister

NEW DELHI: Pralhad Venkatesh Joshi, the new Union education minister, is one of BJP's most experienced parliamentarians and has been in PM Narendra Modi's Cabinet since 2019. The five-time MP from Karnataka also served as president of BJP's Karnataka unit and played a key role in expanding party's footprint in the state before coming to the Centre.Known for his low-profile yet effective style, Joshi has handled important parliamentary and ministerial responsibilities over the years. Before his latest assignment as education minister, he was in charge of consumer affairs, food and public distribution, and new and renewable energy ministries, portfolios that will stay with him.In 2019, he was sworn-in as cabinet minister and given charge of the portfolios of parliamentary affairs, coal and mines until 2024. As parliamentary affairs minister, he handled the passage of key legislation, including the abrogation of Article 370 and the Women's Reservation Bill."Under the guidance of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, I will work to the best of my ability and fulfil my responsibilities with dedication," Joshi told reporters.
Article Summary: Pralhad joshi has been in pm narendra modi's cabinet since 2019. Five-time mp from karnataka also served as president of bjp's karnataka unit. Joshi handled the passage of key legislation, including the abrogation of article 370.

Article Title: Opposition eyes Ayodhya to corner government as end of CJP stir deprives it of an incendiary issue
Article Text:
After Pradhan's exit, opposition set to take up Ayodhya Ram Temple donation theft issue

NEW DELHI: The opposition may have lost a politically incendiary issue with the end of the youth protest, but it is set to move to another controversy that has rocked the country - the Ayodhya donation theft.When the Parliament session started, the alleged Ram Janmabhoomi embezzlement was listed as the top item to target BJP - before the eruption of the youth protest decisively shifted the focus.The aftermath of the paper leak agitation will continue to form the backdrop of what transpires in the coming week. Rahul Gandhi said the opposition holds home minister Amit Shah "directly responsible" for authorising "lethal weapons" against students. "That is going to be a major issue in Parliament," he said.He also demanded that PM Narendra Modi apologise to students.INDIA bloc-plus will Monday brainstorm on the next course of action in view of Modi govt seeking to bring a bill on fast-track courts for paper leaks.The anti-BJP camp has been pushing for a discussion on leaks, and govt had shown an inclination to accept an "adjournment motion". But now, sources said, it is possible that govt will push to club the two.But once the paper leak row is put to bed, sources said the opposition will train its focus on Ayodhya . Congress and SP have been adamant on taking it up, and it has also caught the fancy of other allies like the Left.The anti-BJP camp views the row as a potent weapon to corner the governing party on its home turf of Hindu faith, especially with the embroiling of RSS, VHP and the handpicked temple trust in the row. With elections due in UP and Uttarakhand in early 2027, the opposition is hopeful it will help them with majority community voters.It is not clear how the opposition wants to address the issue - if it wants a normal discussion or would push for an "adjournment motion" that govt would be reluctant to accept because of its symbolic significance and practical implications.Strategists are keeping an eye on the Indo-US trade deal, which has drawn criticism from farmers' groups for concessions made on the agriculture front in the framework agreement. Any movement on the issue could trigger protests, which the opposition would like to seize upon. The controversy over ethanol fuel is also high on the opposition's agenda.
Article Summary: After pradhan's exit, opposition set to take up ayodhya ram temple donation theft issue. India bloc-plus will monday brainstorm on the next course of action in view of modi govt seeking to bring a bill on fast-track courts for paper leaks.

Article Title: From one paper leak protest to another: Full circle for Dharmendra Pradhan
Article Text:
The architect of BJP’s maiden victory in Odisha was first catapulted into the limelight while leadingan ABVP-backed agitation in 1996

Reforms in education under Pradhan

NEW DELHI/BHUBANESWAR: Dharmendra Pradhan 's resignation Saturday marks an unusual stumble in a political career that appeared to be headed towards more important destinations.The architect of BJP's maiden victory in Odisha and facilitator of a series of wins elsewhere was first catapulted into the limelight while leading an ABVP-backed agitation in 1996 against an alleged Class XII question paper leak in Od-isha, during which he was injured in a police lathicharge.Four years later, he won the Pallahara assembly seat on a BJP ticket. He became president of BJP's youth wing, BJYM, in Odisha in 2001 and was elevated as party national secretary in 2002. In 2004, he was appointed BJYM national president.It was also the year he first entered Lok Sabha from Deogarh, when BJP and BJD were allies. Disappointment followed when he lost the assembly poll from Pallahara in 2009 after delimitation abolished the Deogarh LS seat and the alliance collapsed.Pradhan made a comeback when he was appointed co-in-charge of BJP's campaign for 2010 Bihar assembly polls, which BJP swept along with JDU. His nomination to Rajya Sabha from Bihar was seen as a just reward. As election in-charge of Bihar for the 2014 LS polls, he was crucial to NDA's sweep of 31 of its 40 LS seats.In 2014 he was inducted into Modi's first cabinet as MoS with independent charge of the petroleum ministry, despite resistance.Three years later, he was cabinet minister.Amid the controversy over gas pricing, Pradhan launched a clean-up drive and put an end to the complete drip of corporate houses in the sector. His ministry's Ujjwala scheme helped expand LPG access. His work helped him get the education portfolio in 2021.Pradhan's background as a grassroots worker also made him a crucial player in political battles. In 2022, he was made the party's election in-charge in UP, where BJP won 255 of 403 seats. In 2024, he successfully contested from Sambalpur. Though he retained the education ministry in Modi's third term, the reward was seen as less than what he deserved, considering he was the architect of BJP's organisational base in Odisha - a state where the party swept to office for the first time.But things have been challenging for him since then, with paper leaks in 2024 and 2026, as well as the botched-up OMR rollout by CBSE.In between, he delivered a success in Haryana in 2024, and Bihar, where he was BJP's election in-charge in 2025.
Article Summary: The architect of bjp’s maiden victory in odisha was first catapulted into the limelight while leading an abvp-backed agitation in 1996. Pradhan was inducted into modi's first cabinet as mos with independent charge of the petroleum ministry in 2014.

Article Title: 'Country, youth & students far more important than any post': Amit Shah on Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as education minister
Article Text:
Amit Shah reacted to Pradhan's exit, says 'government respects sentiments of country's youth'

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Saturday reacted to Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, saying the BJP considers the country, youth and students more important than any position while reaffirming the Modi government's commitment to reforms against paper leaks.In a post on X, Shah said, "For BJP workers, the country, our youth, and students are far more important than any position. Today, the resignation of Union Education Minister Shri Dharmendra Pradhan ji from his post exemplifies this very principle."Shah further added that the government respected the sentiments of students and remained committed to introducing reforms to prevent paper leaks, while expressing confidence that those responsible would be punished and justice would be ensured for NEET aspirants."The Modi government respects the sentiments of the country's youth and is committed to implementing the necessary reforms against paper leaks. The decisions taken by Modi ji to ensure strict punishment for those guilty of paper leaks are commendable. I am fully confident that these steps will ensure complete justice for the students who succeeded in the NEET examination."He further highlighted Pradhan's tenure as education minister, crediting him with advancing several key education initiatives, including the implementation of the National Education Policy (NEP), expansion of examinations in mother tongues, PM SHRI Schools, digital education, skill development and industry-academia collaboration."During his tenure, Shri Dharmendra Pradhan ji has brought about significant reforms in the effective implementation of the National Education Policy (NEP), arrangements for examinations in mother tongues, expansion of PM SHRI Schools, promotion of digital education, skill development, and strengthening industry-academia coordination. His efforts toward making the examination system more inclusive and student-centric have also been noteworthy. His tenure is a testament to his dedication to the resolve of making India a developed nation."Read more: Dharmendra Pradhan out, Pralhad Joshi in; CJP exits Jantar Mantar, exam reform Bill to enter LS - key points Earlier on Saturday, Shah had also visited Pradhan's residence along with finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman and commerce and industries minister Piyush Goyal, as mark of solidarity.Pradhan resigned as Union education minister earlier on Saturday, amid nationwide protests over NEET-UG paper leak controversy. Hours later, senior BJP leader Pralhad Joshi was given additional charge of the education ministry, while the Centre reached an agreement with the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), leading to the withdrawal of its protest after 36 days at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.
Article Summary: Amit shah reacted to dharmendra pradhan's exit, says 'government respects sentiments of country's youth' he reaffirmed the modi government's commitment to reforms against paper leaks. Shah said the government remained committed to introducing reforms to prevent paper leaks while expressing confidence that those responsible would be punished.

Article Title: Congress was wary of CJP but later joined it in hailing victory
Article Text:
Protests end at Jantar Mantar

NEW DELHI: If the students' protest held the Modi govt hostage for a week, its potency was amplified by the political class that blockaded the Parliament alongside.But the symphony was not perfect from the start as the anti-BJP bloc had two opposing streams. The one led by Congress viewed CJP with suspicion, haunted as it was by the spectre of the Anna Hazare agitation that became the nemesis of the Manmohan govt and was later found to have been orchestrated by RSS. But Left outfits and some regional parties backed CJP as the voice of the youth.When the like-minded parties met an hour before the start of the monsoon session Monday, the NEET protest competed with "Ayodhya donation scam" row as the plank to be espoused.Congress and SP argued that Ayodhya should be picked as the opening salvo against BJP. But a consensus emerged on taking up the "paper leak" protest first after a forceful push from other parties which argued that the opposition had to associate itself with the youth march to Parliament.For Congress, which had been protesting against "paper leaks" for two years, the issue of political credit was also a consideration. The AAP background of CJP founders Abhijeet Dipke and others made many sniff a conspiracy. But barely two hours later, the police crackdown on young marchers ended all equivocation.All along, protesters were also actively courting political support. Activist Sonam Wangchuk , and later his wife Gitanjali Angmo, questioned Rahul's absence from Jantar Mantar, even as SP's Dimple and Akhilesh Yadav, Shiv Sena's Uddhav Thackeray and son Aditya, NCP-SP's Sharad Pawar, AAP's Arvind Kejriwal and scores of others visited the venue.CPI (ML)'s Dipankar Bhattacharya and CPM's M A Baby were among the first to lend support in early June.Post-crackdown, the gap kept closing as the controversy intensified, crowds continued to swell and the story went global.Amid scepticism about the newbie, Congress and opposition were assured by the fact that the Jantar Mantar stage of Dipke had been filled with student activists from the Left parties. It was evident in the way Rahul Saturday held a news conference with AISA activists to reiterate that protesters would not budge without the resignation of the education minister. It appeared to be a bid to queer the pitch for CJP, which was in talks with govt.In the end, as Dharmendra Pradhan resigned, the political class and the Jantar Mantar platform were together in hailing it as a victory for the young seeking accountability from the govt.
Article Summary: The anti-bjp bloc had two opposing streams. The one led by congress viewed cjp with suspicion. Left outfits and some regional parties backed cjp as the voice of the youth. The police crackdown on young marchers ended all equivocation.

Article Title: Amit Shah & other top BJP functionaries call on Pradhan at his residence to show solidarity
Article Text:
BJP figures, including home minister Amit Shah, visited Dharmendra Pradhan’s residence in a show of solidarity after he resigned

NEW DELHI: A steady stream of leading BJP figures, including home minister Amit Shah , visited Dharmendra Pradhan 's residence in a show of solidarity after he resigned as education minister owing to student protests over the NEET paper leak.Besides Shah, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman and commerce and industries minister Piyush Goyal were among the key Union Cabinet members who met Pradhan, who has handled crucial political assignments, including state elections.Shah said Pradhan helmed "bold reforms" by implementing NEP, placing emphasis on mother tongues, and making exams more inclusive and student-centric. He added, however, that the country and the young generation were more important to BJP than any office, saying, "Modi govt respects the youth's sentiments and is committed to necessary reforms against paper leaks."Party president Nitin Nabin said BJP "stood firmly" with Pradhan."He played a pivotal role in reforming India's education landscape and successfully implementing the landmark NEP... Prioritising larger interests, his decision to step down reflects the highest standards of integrity and selfless service in public life," Nabin added.The tributes are a firm indication that Pradhan remains a valuable figure for BJP despite his exit owing to political necessities.Defence minister Rajnath Singh said Pradhan's tenure reflected his commitment to transforming India into a developed nation. "His contribution to public service has been inclusive, foresighted, and aligned with the aspirations of a new India," he added.Another ministerial colleague, Kiren Rijiju, praised Pradhan for his dedication to strengthening India's education ecosystem. "Leading such a critical sector demands immense persever-ance, and he embraced it with courage and clear vision," he said.
Article Summary: Bjp figures, including home minister amit shah, visited dharmendra pradhan’s residence in a show of solidarity after he resigned as education minister owing to neet paper leak. Party president nitin nabin said bjp "stood firmly" withpradhan.

Article Title: Dharmendra Pradhan out, Pralhad Joshi in: CJP exits Jantar Mantar, exam reform Bill to enter LS - key points
Article Text:
CJP protestors and students celebrate after Pradhan's resignation

Here are the top developments:

Pralhad Joshi gets additional charge of education ministry

Metro stations reopen after protest ends

Pradhan resigns, cites moral responsibility

Centre and CJP reach agreement after third round of talks

Student movement ends after 36 days

Opposition calls it a victory for students

Wangchuk welcomes outcome

Tougher anti-paper leak law proposed

Biggest political fallout of NEET controversy

NEW DELHI: Saturday witnessed a series of major developments in the NEET paper leak controversy, beginning with Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation after weeks of nationwide protests.Hours later, Pralhad Joshi was appointed as the new education minister getting additional charge apart from portfolios of new and renewable energy and consumer affairs, food and public distribution.Meanwhile, the Centre and the Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) held a third round of talks, after which the government agreed to withdraw FIRs filed against peaceful protesters.Following the meeting, the CJP announced the immediate withdrawal of its 36-day agitation at Jantar Mantar, saying it was ending the protest in "good faith" after the government accepted its key demands.The protest site was cleared after the CJP demands were met.The developments marked the biggest political fallout of the NEET controversy, which triggered nationwide student protests, a CBI probe and sweeping reforms to India's examination system.Hours after Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, President Droupadi Murmu assigned senior BJP leader Pralhad Joshi the additional charge of the Union education ministry on the advice of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.A five-time Lok Sabha MP from Karnataka's Dharwad, Joshi will continue to hold the portfolios of new and renewable energy and consumer affairs, food and public distribution. He takes charge at a crucial time as the government rolls out reforms following the NEET-UG paper leak, including restructuring the NTA, tightening exam security and shifting NEET to computer-based testing from 2027.After being given the charge, Joshi said: "The Prime Minister has placed his trust in me and has entrusted me with such a significant responsibility. With complete humility and a strong sense of responsibility, I will fulfil this duty...I thank the Prime Minister for giving me this important responsibility and for showing such great confidence in me. Under his guidance and leadership, I will work sincerely and try my best to meet his expectations in this department. With full dedication, humility, and honesty, I will work towards fulfilling this responsibility. I once again thank the Prime Minister for giving me this opportunity."Normal Metro access resumed across Delhi after the CJP called off its 36-day protest, with the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) reopening the entry gates of all stations that had been closed because of security arrangements.The reopening came shortly after Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned and the Centre reached an agreement with the CJP to end the agitation.Earlier in the day, the DMRC had resumed services at Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House and Central Secretariat stations before restoring entry and exit at all 18 affected stations, which had been placed under restrictions due to the protests near Jantar Mantar.Announcing his resignation in a letter addressed to the country's youth, Pradhan said he had submitted his resignation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi after considering the situation that had developed at Jantar Mantar and across the country.He said he had spent more than four decades working for students, teachers and education reforms and had always believed that a strong education system was the foundation of a strong nation. Pradhan said the government acted immediately after irregularities surfaced in the NEET-UG examination by handing the investigation to the CBI, cancelling the examination and announcing a fresh test, while also deciding to shift NEET to computer-based mode from next year.He added that he had accepted responsibility from the very beginning and had worked to ensure that no deserving student suffered because of what he described as an examination mafia.Recalling the events of the past few days had deeply saddened him, Pradhan said he was stepping down to prevent anti-national forces from exploiting the situation, safeguard national unity and allow students to focus on their education.Hours after Pradhan's resignation, the Centre and the Cockroach Janta Party held a third round of talks, following which the student group announced the immediate withdrawal of its 36-day protest.Addressing a joint press conference with Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, CJP spokespersons Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das said the agitation was being withdrawn in good faith after the government accepted its key demands.The CJP said its primary demand, Pradhan's resignation, had been fulfilled. It also said the Centre had agreed to withdraw FIRs and legal cases against peaceful protesters and assured that no retaliatory action would be taken.The government further agreed to provide compensation to the families of students who died by suicide in accordance with existing rules and regulations and promised to consider the CJP's five-point charter on examination reforms.JP Nadda said the government had sympathetically considered the delegation's demands and would hold further discussions on long-term reforms to strengthen the examination system.The CJP protest began at Jantar Mantar on June 20, demanding accountability over the alleged NEET-UG paper leak, wider reforms in the examination system and Pradhan's resignation.The movement gained national attention after climate activist Sonam Wangchuk joined the agitation with an indefinite hunger strike. His deteriorating health and later hospitalisation intensified public attention and increased pressure on the government.Although Wangchuk ended his 26-day fast after receiving written assurances from the Centre, the CJP continued its protest until Pradhan resigned and the remaining demands were addressed.Speaking after the agreement, Ashutosh Ranka appealed to protesters across the country to withdraw peacefully, while Saurav Das said the movement was ending with the understanding that all commitments would be implemented within the agreed timelines."Government accepted all our demands after 36 days of protest; we urge everyone to peacefully withdraw from protest sites," CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka said.Earlier in the day, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke had briefly said the protest would continue until all demands were accepted. After the talks concluded, however, the organisation announced the end of the agitation.Dipke also urged supporters not to treat Pradhan's resignation as a personal victory for him, saying the movement was driven by thousands of young people and should remain focused on institutional reforms rather than individuals.Amit Shah reacts to Pradhan's exitUnion home minister Amit Shah reacted to Dharmendra Pradhan's exit as education minister saying, "Modi government respects youth's sentiments"."For BJP workers, the country, our youth, and students are far more important than any position. Today, the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan ji from his post exemplifies this very principle. The Modi government respects the sentiments of the country's youth and is committed to implementing the necessary reforms against paper leaks. The decisions taken by Modi ji to ensure strict punishment for those guilty of paper leaks are commendable. I am fully confident that these steps will ensure complete justice for the students who succeeded in the NEET examination.," he said."During his tenure, Shri Dharmendra Pradhan ji has brought about significant reforms in the effective implementation of the National Education Policy (NEP), arrangements for examinations in mother tongues, expansion of PM SHRI Schools, promotion of digital education, skill development, and strengthening industry-academia coordination. His efforts toward making the examination system more inclusive and student-centric have also been noteworthy. His tenure is a testament to his dedication to the resolve of making India a developed nation," he added.The opposition described Pradhan's resignation as a major victory for students and renewed calls for broader reforms in the education system.Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi called the resignation "the victory of the future of India", saying Pradhan had become a symbol of corruption, incompetence and the decline of the country's education system.He said the government must now introduce meaningful reforms and alleged that the issue of police action against student protesters would remain a key matter during the Monsoon Session of Parliament.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge termed the resignation a "victory of truth" and said Prime Minister Narendra Modi should apologise to the country's youth while ensuring action against those responsible for the alleged use of force against protesters.AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal described the development as a "big win for democracy", while Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar said the Congress would continue raising issues concerning students and maintained that peaceful protests were an essential part of democracy.Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk welcomed the developments, describing them as "a victory of democracy, direct democracy, peace, patience and perseverance". He congratulated the student movement and thanked citizens across the country for supporting the agitation.His wife, Gitanjali Angmo, also praised the role played by India's younger generation, saying the protests had demonstrated courage, patriotism and commitment to democratic values without violence.The Centre has proposed major amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act to ensure faster investigations, time-bound trials and stricter punishment for paper leaks and examination malpractice.The proposed Bill provides for the creation of Special Task Forces (STFs) to investigate offences, completion of investigations within two months, day-to-day hearings in special fast-track courts and disposal of appeals by High Courts within three months.It also significantly increases penalties, proposing jail terms of up to 10 years and fines of up to Rs 10 crore for organised paper leak rackets, along with tougher action against service providers and officials found involved in examination fraud.Pradhan's resignation marks the most significant political consequence of the NEET-UG paper leak controversy, which began after allegations of question paper leaks in the May 3 examination.The controversy led to the cancellation of the examination, a nationwide CBI investigation, repeated protests, parliamentary disruptions, changes to the anti-paper leak law and a major restructuring of the National Testing Agency.Pradhan also removed education minister from his X bio following the resignation.
Article Summary: Pralhad joshi gets additional charge of education ministry. Centre and cockroach janta party ( cjp) reach agreement after third round of talks. Cjp announces immediate withdrawal of its 36-day agitation at jantar mantar. Dharmendra pradhan steps down as education minister. Centre and cockroach janta party hold third round of talks.

Article Title: Ram Temple donation theft row: UP govt reconstitutes SIT; IG Kiran S to lead probe
Article Text:
UP govt reconstitutes SIT probing Ram Temple donation theft row after SC orders

NEW DELHI: Acting on the Supreme Court's directions, the Uttar Pradesh government has constituted a new Special Investigation Team (SIT) led by senior IPS officers to investigate the alleged embezzlement of devotees' offerings at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple in Ayodhya.The reconstituted team is headed by Inspector General Kiran S, with Deputy Inspector General Somen Verma and Ayodhya Senior Superintendent of Police Dr Gaurav Grover as members. It replaces the earlier SIT, which was headed by Lucknow Commissioner Vijay Vishwas Pant and included Special Secretary (Finance) Neel Ratan Kumar among its members.The apex court had, during a July 13 hearing, expressed the view that allegations involving theft and financial irregularities required investigation by experienced police officers.A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohan directed the state to form a fresh SIT under a senior IPS officer and submit a status report by July 27.The case centres on allegations that offerings made by devotees at the Ram temple were siphoned off instead of being deposited through the prescribed process.Investigators probing the case earlier examined CCTV footage, donation registers, cash-handling records and financial documents, besides questioning temple staff.Their preliminary findings indicated suspected irregularities in the counting and deposit of donations.The investigation led to the arrest of several accused, while police seized cash, vehicles, investment documents and other assets allegedly acquired using the misappropriated funds. Investigators also analysed bank transactions and other digital evidence to trace the alleged money trail.With the new SIT now taking over the probe, the Uttar Pradesh government is expected to place its findings before the Supreme Court in a status report on July 27.
Article Summary: Up govt reconstitutes sit probing ram temple donation theft row after sc orders it. Case centres on allegations that offerings made by devotees at the ram temple were siphoned off. Uttar pradesh government expected to place its findings before the supreme court in a status report on july 27.

Article Title: Students protest: Gen Z forces DP Change
Article Text:
Protesters at Jantar Mantar celebrate news of Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation

Why BJP chose to cut its losses

NEW DELHI: Dharmendra Pradhan, who earned his early spurs by leading a protest against a Class 12 question paper leak in Odisha in 1996 as an ABVP national secretary, was forced to resign Saturday as Union education minister, in the face of unrelenting protests fuelled by students’ anger over NEET-UG paper leak.Govt conceded to the key demand of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and the opposition as Pradhan sent his resignation to PM Modi, in an unprecedented ouster of a cabinet minister of his govt for over 12 years, marking a political setback to BJP and a rare boost for its rivals.Five-time Karnataka MP and Union minister Pralhad Joshi, who holds several other portfolios, has been given additional charge of education.Jubilant CJP members, led by its founder Abhijeet Dipke, called off their agitation after a third round of talks with Union ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh.“Democracy wins,” CJP said on X.CJP spokesperson Saurav Das announced withdrawal of protests with immediate effect at a news conference, where both ministers wore a resigned look. Govt has also agreed to provide “honourable” compensation to families of NEET candidates who died by suicide and withdraw FIRs against protesting students in Delhi and other BJP-governed states, he added.The two sides will again meet after four weeks to work on broader reforms in the exam system, CJP said.In a two-page statement, Pradhan said he has quit so that “anti-national forces do not take advantage of the situation” at Jantar Mantar and across the country”. It is not a matter of personal prestige, he said.His statement was addressed to “my young friends”, a nod to Gen Z, who have been the face of CJP-led protests, and left the all-powerful BJP searching for answers to their unconventional onslaught. A govt functionary said largescale participation of youth gave the campaign, which BJP initially saw as sponsored by AAP and Left-aligned groups, an emotive undercurrent, leaving them little choice but to retreat as the protest grew.For a party which rarely makes any concession to rivals on their terms and exudes an air of bold strength rooted in popular endorsement in polls, BJP’s decision to bow to the student protest also reflects the pragmatism it has shown when confronted with street agitation — better to cut losses than let the pain fester into a more serious challenge.In Nov 2021, Modi had announced withdrawal of farm laws in the face of over a yearlong protest by farmers, which was largely confined to Punjab and parts of Haryana and western UP but had remained stubborn. The PM, too, had ascribed the decision to national interest, which observers thought was a reference to the sensitivity of Punjab as a border state.Pradhan’s mention of the stir at Jantar Mantar but no acknowledgement of Congressled opposition’s protest, which has kept Parliament’s monsoon session deadlocked, is seemingly aimed at denying any credit to BJP’s political rivals while conceding to CJP, which is not really an electoral threat.With Rahul Gandhi, too, stepping up his agitation— his surprise demonstration outside Modi’s residence on July 21 was a highlight — so as not to allow CJP, seen closer to its ‘secular’ rival AAP, hog the limelight, Congress is bound to lay claim to the credit. However, BJP has more often than not seen off its challenge without much political damage.There was sympathy in the ranks for Pradhan who, as petroleum minister, rolled out the vote-spinner Ujjwala scheme and stayed engaged with the cadre. He had a stream of visitors — home minister Amit Shah and finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman included.“We had to swallow the bitter pill because there was a real risk of violence breaking out. Any loss of lives would have been blamed on us. Moreover, it was about students and their families,” said a senior minister.The sense of resignation was accompanied by surprise as to why the leadership did not take measures it subsequently took to tackle the discontent: strengthening of the law against paper leaks, eviction of key bureaucrats from education ministry, drastic action against NTA officials, and Pradhan’s resignation.In his statement, Pradhan, 57, who took charge of education ministry in July 2021, emphasised his decades-long commitment to students and education, and said he took responsibility of the fallout of the NEET-UG paper leak from the very first day.The re-exam result was declared on time, and many poor meritorious students made the cut, he said, while blaming those in responsible positions, alikely swipe at Rahul and other key opposition figures, for trying to mislead students.The BJP brass expressed its full backing for Pradhan, a deft politician who has been the choice of Modi and Shah in helming numerous state elections, as he stepped down. BJP president Nitin Nabin credited him for key reforms and lauded him for prioritising larger interests, in keeping with “the highest standards of integrity and selfless service in public life”.
Article Summary: Dharmendra pradhan resigned as union education minister on saturday. His ouster marks a political setback to bjp and a rare boost for its rivals. Cjp members, led by its founder abhijeet dipke, called off their agitation after a third round of talks.

Article Title: Govt had to bow before collective struggle of youth, says opposition
Article Text:
Opposition react to Pradhan's exit

NEW DELHI: Following Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, opposition parties Saturday said this marked a victory of democracy and said Modi govt had to "bow before the collective struggle" of the country's youth. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said the youth compelled BJP to bow before their pressure, and also started the countdown to its "ouster from power". "The issue is not limited to one minister or one exam, but reflects a larger breakdown of trust among job aspirants who spend years preparing for competitive exams," he said, calling for strict accountability.NCP-SP chief Sharad Pawar said the resignation was a major victory for youth power.Earlier this week, he met the protesting youths at Jantar Mantar in Delhi. He also met PM Modi a day after."I personally met the PM and told him that dialogue was essential in democracy. If dialogue does not take place, it leads to adverse consequences. I urged the PM to depute senior colleagues to hold talks. I had also told protesters that they should go ahead with talks if govt shows willingness to discuss their demands," Pawar said."Couple of rounds of talks took place. Some of the demands of youths were accepted, they were pressing for the minister's resignation," he said.TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee said, "People in power must realise that power of the people is greater than any office or authority. One can love their country deeply without having to love govt of the day."While Sena UBT president Uddhav Thackeray said, "A single cockroach made a dictator bow down", MNS chief Raj Thackeray said, "Gen Z has uprooted govt's hair. And brought it down to earth."The development has restored people's faith in democracy by proving that govts must ultimately listen to people's voice, AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal said.
Article Summary: Opposition parties say dharmendra pradhan's resignation is a victory of democracy. Samajwadi party chief akhilesh yadav said the youth compelled bjp to bow before their pressure. Ncp-sp chief sharad pawar said the resignation was a major victory for youth power.

Article Title: Left scores win, despite its shrunken presence, through its student organs
Article Text:
When the Left-aligned student groups joined the CJP-led protest, they were drawn into the fold organically, said parties’ functionaries

NEW DELHI: It must qualify as a striking case of maximising one's returns on meagre capital. Disproportionate to its marginal presence in Parliament and anaemic strength on the ground, Left parties successfully leveraged AISA, SFI and AISF, which have active units in Delhi, to pressure govt to give into the demand of getting Dharmendra Pradhan to resign as education minister.In fact, AISA members, president Neha Bora and Manish Kumar and Ameen Amitoj, despite having no prior association with Abhijeet Dipke, sat on a 23-day hunger strike in solidarity with the students.The victory of their student outfits, which made common cause with those sections of Gen Z, who are usually not receptive to their "class warfare" trope, could act as a compensation of sorts for the Left in an electorally bleak season, marked by routs in Kerala and West Bengal.Earlier, in another instance of them successfully using their tactical intelligence, the Left, through its farmers' wings, influenced the protests in Punjab against farm sector reforms laws enacted by Modi govt, which had to junk them.If AISA, SFI and AISF were a vocal presence throughout the protest, their mother outfits CPI(ML), CPM and CPI, in that order, complemented the effort on the ground by goading the opposition to support the CJP-led protests.According to Left functionaries, who have been part of the demonstrations, when the Left-aligned students groups joined the students' protest led by CJP, they were drawn into the fold organically and not perceived as people just jumping in for credit as these students have been raising issues around the flaws in the examination system and the challenges through their unions.All 15 MPs belonging to the Left joined the students to protest the police action against them during the march to Parliament on July 20. They also ensured there was no dilution of the demand for Pradhan's resignation.CPI(ML) general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya agreed that the success of the protests has given the Left a fillip. "This movement has re-energised ongoing struggles across the country for democracy, justice, and the defence of the Constitution." He called upon INDIA bloc to carry the energy, resolve, and democratic spirit of this movement into Parliament and intensify the struggle for affordable and quality education for all.CPM general secretary M A Baby said Pradhan's resignation was the first step. "Congratulations to Abhijeet Dipke and CJP, to SFI, AISF, AISA, and lakhs of students and young people for their courage and determination which has won this historic victory. We demand comprehensive reform: scrap NTA! Take back NEP!" CPM said."It is a rare moment of democratic accountability, achieved not through the goodwill of an arrogant govt, but through the sustained struggle of students and youth across the country. The students' movement has defeated the arrogance of BJP and compelled the Modi-Shah regime to answer for its failures," CPI general secretary D Raja said.
Article Summary: Left parties leveraged aisa, sfi and aisf, which have active units in delhi. Victory could act as compensation of sorts for the left in an electorally bleak season. Aisa members, despite having no prior association with abhijeet dipke, sat on a 23-day hunger strike.

Article Title: PM Modi is India's past, protesting youth the country's future, says Rahul
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi said "past can never fight the future”.

NEW DELHI: Asserting that "time has come to remove this govt", Congress 's Rahul Gandhi said PM Narendra Modi is India's past while the protesting youth are the country's future. He added that the "past can never fight the future". Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge called education minister Dharmendra Pradhan 's resignation a "victory of truth and defeat of Modi's stubbornness".Rahul said students' agitation has issued a warning that if BJP-RSS continue to run the govt like their personal fiefdom, they would face a stir 10 times more intense than what is happening now. He accused RSS of hollowing India from inside like termites. He said Pradhan's resignation is a signal to other communities that are being "oppressed" by Modi govt, that fighting the govt is a wise step.Wayanad MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra said, "Force was used against them.But the youth did not bend; govt had to bend." She said she had been wondering for the past 10-12 years, "When will we wake up and realise what is being done to our country?" She said the youth are reclaiming their country.Party MP K C Venugopal said, "A massive salute to millions of students across country who compelled this govt to bow down to their will."Rahul said that Pradhan was a symbol of corruption and destruction of world-class education system, and "it is good that he is gone".
Article Summary: Rahul said students' agitation has issued a warning that if bjp-rss continue to run the govt like their personal fiefdom, they would face a stir 10 times more intense than what is happening now. Congress president mallikarjun kharge called education minister dharmendra pradhan's resignation a "victory of truth"

Article Title: Bill proposes 3-month deadline for HCs to dispose of paper leak appeals
Article Text:
Bid to make investigation and judicial process time-bound

What changes in New Bill

NEW DELHI: Aiming to ensure faster disposal of exam paper leak cases, govt has proposed a three-month deadline for respective high courts to dispose of appeals against orders of special fast-track courts, unlike other cases where no such fixed timeline for deciding appeals exists. This converts an open-ended investigation and judicial process into a time-bound one.According to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill circulated to Lok Sabha MPs Saturday, individuals, service providers and organised gangs involved in paper leaks would face longer jail terms, steeper fines, and time-bound investigation and disposal of trials and appeals.As per the bill, which would be introduced in Lok Sabha Monday, the minimum jail term for offences committed by individuals, as well as directors, senior management personnel or persons in charge of service providers conducting public examinations, has been increased to five years.In cases involving organised crime, the minimum imprisonment has been proposed at seven years from the current provision of five years. In all these cases, the maximum jail term would be 10 years.For speedy investigations, the bill proposes govt may constitute a central investigation agency or a special task force (STF). Where an STF has been constituted, it would carry out the investigation. The bill also seeks to insert a new provision mandating that every investigation be completed within two months.The bill provides for day-to-day proceedings and empowers states to establish special fast-track courts in consultation with the chief justice of the respective HC.It mandates that such trial proceedings shall continue until all witnesses in attendance have been examined. These courts would be required to dispose of cases within three months from the date of filing of the chargesheet. All pending trials will be shifted to the special court, and these must also be disposed of within three months.It proposes that any appeal against an order of a fast-track court shall be heard by a division bench of HC. It proposes that every appeal be filed within 30 days from the date of the fast-track court's order and not after a maximum of 90 days under any circumstances.
Article Summary: Public examinations (prevention of unfair means) amendment bill circulated to lok sabha mps saturday. Individuals, service providers and organised gangs involved in paper leaks would face longer jail terms, steeper fines, and time-bound investigation and disposal of trials and appeals.
